title: Avimi bar Nazi
author: Aharon Hyman

paragraphs: He was Ravina’s father-in-law—it should read Ravnai’s father-in-law. [Bava Kamma 115a](https://www.sefaria.org/Bava_Kamma.115a.22-24) relates that someone owed him four zuz. The case came before Ravina (it should read Ravnai); Rav Kohen objected, and the matter eventually reached Rabbi Abbahu. Hyman argues that this shows Ravnai is intended, since in Rabbi Abbahu’s time Ravina had not yet been born or was a small child. [The Rif](https://www.sefaria.org/Rif_Bava_Kamma.42a.6) reads “Abaye bar Nazi, Ravina’s father-in-law,” and says that the matter eventually reached Rava. Hyman calls this a scribal error: “eventually reached” implies that it came in time to the Land of Israel, whereas Rava was in Mahoza and Ravina was before him.

notes.text: The checked passage names Rav Kohen, not Rav Kahana. Ravnai in place of Ravina and Abaye in place of Avimi are Hyman’s reported or proposed readings. His explanation of the chronology and travel of the case is not an independent historical finding.

The Gemara and [Heilprin’s entry](https://www.girsology.com/seder-hadorot.html?entry=153&lang=en) have Avimi, Ravina, Rav Kohen and Rabbi Abbahu. The linked Rif has Abaye and ends with Rava, as Hyman reports, but calls Abaye “Rabbi’s father-in-law.” The Rif’s text also names Ravina as the judge first approached. Hyman’s Ravnai proposal and his argument about how the case travelled remain his own.
